chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from his father from Hammad ibn Isa from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

There is no believer who helps an oppressed believer except that it is better than fasting for a month and performing i'tikaf in the Sacred Mosque. And there is no believer who supports his brother while he is capable of supporting him except that Allah supports him in the world and the hereafter. And there is no believer who abandons his brother while he is capable of supporting him except that Allah abandons him in the world and the hereafter.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for helping an oppressed believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the immense virtue of *nasr al-mu'min* (supporting the believer), equating the act of aiding an oppressed brother to the cumulative reward of a month of fasting and *i'tikaf* in the Sacred Mosque, a metric that underscores its priority over solitary worship. This narration establishes a reciprocal divine covenant where active support guarantees Allah's aid in both the worldly and afterlife realms, while neglect invites divine abandonment, reflecting the Shia emphasis on communal solidarity (*ta'awun*) as a core spiritual duty.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. My father (rah) said: it was narrated to me by Sa’d b. Abdillah from Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah from his father from Hamad b. Isa from Ibrahim b. Umar al-Yamani from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “

One who helps an oppressed believer its reward is better than that of fasting for a month and performing Etekaf in Masjidul Haraam. One who is capable of helping a Muslim and helps him, the Almighty Allah will help him in the world and the hereafter. If a believer is being backbited and a person capable of helping him remains silent and does not defend him, the Almighty Allah will make him deprived in the world and the hereafter.”
